neighbours.label: the punctuation or 'and' right after a spoken self-introduction 'I'm <Name>' (I'm Scott Simon. / I'm Remus, …); third-person naming and 'I'm <adjective>' stay quiet
fire: Welcome back to the evening bulletin. I'm Paula Reyes. Rain is expected across the north tonight.
He set down his bag and smiled. "I'm Gideon, Gideon Marsh. We spoke on the phone."
Hello everyone! I'm Priya Nair, and I teach pottery classes on weekends.
"Sorry to barge in. I'm Felix. Your sister said I could wait here."
You're listening to City Desk on public radio. I'm Owen Hartley. First, the headlines.
The woman at the door spoke first. "I'm Ingrid, the new tenant from upstairs."
Thanks for joining the webinar. I'm Marcus Bell, and today we'll cover payroll basics.
"Don't be alarmed. I'm Nurse Okafor. You've been asleep for two days."

notes: Card: '.' ',' ' and' after 'I'm <Name>', plus 'What are you?'. Probes: 'I'm Karen Blake.' 0.72, 'I'm Tobias,' 0.72, 'I'm Dana Whitfield, and' 0.98, 'I'm Leo Marsh.' 0.77; 'The reporter was Karen Blake.' 0.18, 'name is Karen Blake.' 0.09, 'I'm exhausted,' 0.09. Also fires on second-person identity ('You're Remy,' 0.72, 'What are you?' 0.89) and weaker on 'He's Tobias,' 0.41, so the label is the first-person core of a broader 'who someone is' pattern.
